questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Corynebacterium, Bacillus, Listeria, Nocardia, Actinomyces
questions.stem: The medium of choice for isolating Corynebacterium diphtheriae is:
options: Loeffler serum slope and potassium tellurite agar
questions.concept: Loeffler serum slope gives rapid growth showing metachromatic volutin granules, while tellurite agar is selective, producing characteristic grey-black colonies. Albert stain demonstrates the granules.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Corynebacterium, Bacillus, Listeria, Nocardia, Actinomyces
questions.stem: Diphtheria toxin acts by:
options: ADP-ribosylating elongation factor 2, halting protein synthesis
questions.concept: The toxin is produced only by strains lysogenised by a tox-gene bearing beta phage. It causes local pseudomembrane formation and systemic myocarditis and neuritis, treated with antitoxin plus antibiotics.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Corynebacterium, Bacillus, Listeria, Nocardia, Actinomyces
questions.stem: The Schick test was historically used to determine:
options: Susceptibility to diphtheria by assessing antitoxin immunity
questions.concept: Intradermal toxin producing erythema indicated absent antitoxin and therefore susceptibility. It is now obsolete, replaced by serological antitoxin assays and universal DPT immunisation.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Corynebacterium, Bacillus, Listeria, Nocardia, Actinomyces
questions.stem: Anthrax is caused by an organism described as:
options: A large aerobic Gram-positive spore-forming bacillus in bamboo-stick chains with a polypeptide capsule
questions.concept: Bacillus anthracis has a unique poly-D-glutamic acid capsule, forms centrally placed spores that survive decades in soil, and gives a medusa-head colony. Cutaneous anthrax produces a painless black eschar.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Corynebacterium, Bacillus, Listeria, Nocardia, Actinomyces
questions.stem: Listeria monocytogenes is particularly dangerous in:
options: Pregnant women, neonates, the elderly and the immunosuppressed
questions.concept: Listeria causes granulomatosis infantiseptica, neonatal meningitis, and meningitis in the immunosuppressed. It grows at refrigeration temperature, shows tumbling motility at 25 degrees, and is intrinsically resistant to cephalosporins - hence ampicillin is added empirically.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Corynebacterium, Bacillus, Listeria, Nocardia, Actinomyces
questions.stem: Actinomyces israelii infection is characterised by:
options: Chronic suppuration with sinus tracts discharging sulphur granules
questions.concept: Actinomycosis is caused by an anaerobic Gram-positive branching filamentous bacterium of normal oral flora, producing cervicofacial, thoracic or abdominal disease with sulphur granules. Prolonged high-dose penicillin is the treatment.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Corynebacterium, Bacillus, Listeria, Nocardia, Actinomyces
questions.stem: Nocardia differs from Actinomyces in being:
questions.concept: Nocardia is an aerobic, weakly acid-fast filamentous bacterium causing pulmonary and brain abscesses in the immunosuppressed and mycetoma after soil inoculation. Cotrimoxazole is the drug of choice.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Corynebacterium, Bacillus, Listeria, Nocardia, Actinomyces
questions.stem: The treatment of diphtheria must include antitoxin because:
options: Antibiotics kill the organism but cannot neutralise toxin already bound to tissue
questions.concept: Antitoxin neutralises only circulating unbound toxin, so it must be given on clinical suspicion without waiting for culture. Penicillin or erythromycin stops further toxin production and eliminates the carrier state.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Corynebacterium, Bacillus, Listeria, Nocardia, Actinomyces
questions.stem: Woolsorter's disease refers to:
options: Pulmonary anthrax from inhalation of spores, with haemorrhagic mediastinitis
questions.concept: Inhalational anthrax causes a widened mediastinum from haemorrhagic mediastinitis with rapid progression to shock and death, and is the form of greatest bioterrorism concern. Ciprofloxacin or doxycycline with antitoxin is used.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Corynebacterium, Bacillus, Listeria, Nocardia, Actinomyces
questions.stem: Bacillus cereus food poisoning classically follows ingestion of:
options: Reheated fried rice, causing a short-incubation emetic syndrome
questions.concept: The heat-stable preformed emetic toxin in rice held at room temperature causes vomiting within 1 to 6 hours, while a heat-labile enterotoxin causes a diarrhoeal syndrome at 8 to 16 hours resembling Clostridium perfringens.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Respiratory viruses: influenza, SARS-CoV-2, measles, mumps, rubella
questions.stem: Antigenic shift in influenza virus refers to:
options: Major reassortment of gene segments producing a new subtype capable of causing pandemics
questions.concept: Shift occurs only in influenza A through reassortment of the segmented RNA genome between human and animal strains, producing pandemics. Antigenic drift is gradual point mutation causing seasonal epidemics and requiring annual vaccine reformulation.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Respiratory viruses: influenza, SARS-CoV-2, measles, mumps, rubella
questions.stem: The influenza surface antigens used in subtype nomenclature are:
questions.concept: Haemagglutinin mediates attachment to sialic acid receptors and is the main neutralising target, while neuraminidase releases progeny virions and is inhibited by oseltamivir and zanamivir.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Respiratory viruses: influenza, SARS-CoV-2, measles, mumps, rubella
questions.stem: Koplik spots, pathognomonic of measles, appear:
options: On the buccal mucosa one to two days before the rash
questions.concept: Koplik spots are grain-of-salt white lesions on an erythematous buccal mucosa appearing in the prodrome, making them useful for early diagnosis and isolation. The rash then spreads cephalocaudally and fades with staining and desquamation.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Respiratory viruses: influenza, SARS-CoV-2, measles, mumps, rubella
questions.stem: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis is a late complication of:
questions.concept: SSPE develops 7 to 10 years after measles, especially when infection occurred under 2 years, with progressive myoclonus, dementia and a characteristic EEG. Measles vaccination has virtually eliminated it.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Respiratory viruses: influenza, SARS-CoV-2, measles, mumps, rubella
questions.stem: The commonest complication of mumps in a postpubertal male is:
options: Orchitis, usually unilateral and rarely causing sterility
questions.concept: Mumps orchitis affects 20 to 30% of postpubertal males, usually unilaterally, and sterility is uncommon. Aseptic meningitis, pancreatitis and sensorineural deafness are other complications.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Respiratory viruses: influenza, SARS-CoV-2, measles, mumps, rubella
questions.stem: Rubella is of greatest clinical importance because of:
options: Congenital rubella syndrome following maternal infection in the first trimester
questions.concept: Rubella is a mild illness with posterior auricular and suboccipital lymphadenopathy, but first-trimester infection causes cataract, deafness and cardiac defects, with risk falling sharply after 16 weeks.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Respiratory viruses: influenza, SARS-CoV-2, measles, mumps, rubella
questions.stem: Measles vaccine is a:
options: Live attenuated vaccine given at 9 months in India with a second dose at 16 to 24 months
questions.concept: Live attenuated measles-rubella vaccine is given at 9 to 12 months and 16 to 24 months under the Indian schedule. It is given subcutaneously and is contraindicated in pregnancy and severe immunodeficiency.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Respiratory viruses: influenza, SARS-CoV-2, measles, mumps, rubella
questions.stem: The principal mode of transmission of SARS-CoV-2 is:
options: Respiratory droplets and aerosols from an infected person
questions.concept: Transmission is predominantly by respiratory particles at close range, with aerosol spread in poorly ventilated indoor spaces, which is why masking, ventilation and distancing are effective. Fomite transmission is possible but minor.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Respiratory viruses: influenza, SARS-CoV-2, measles, mumps, rubella
questions.stem: Respiratory syncytial virus is named for its ability to:
options: Cause fusion of infected cells into multinucleate syncytia
questions.concept: The F (fusion) protein causes cell fusion producing syncytia, and is the target of palivizumab prophylaxis in high-risk infants. RSV is the leading cause of bronchiolitis and infant hospitalisation.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Respiratory viruses: influenza, SARS-CoV-2, measles, mumps, rubella
questions.stem: Oseltamivir is most effective when given:
questions.concept: Neuraminidase inhibitors shorten illness by about a day and reduce complications when started within 48 hours, with greatest benefit in severe disease and high-risk groups where treatment is given regardless of duration.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Helminths: intestinal & tissue nematodes, cestodes, trematodes
questions.stem: Neurocysticercosis results from ingestion of:
options: Eggs of Taenia solium, making humans an accidental intermediate host
questions.concept: Eating undercooked pork containing cysticerci gives intestinal taeniasis, whereas ingesting eggs by the faeco-oral route causes cysticercosis with cysts in brain, muscle and eye - the reason personal hygiene matters more than pork avoidance.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Helminths: intestinal & tissue nematodes, cestodes, trematodes
questions.stem: Hydatid disease is caused by and diagnosed by:
options: Echinococcus granulosus, with the dog as definitive host, diagnosed by imaging and serology
questions.concept: Humans are accidental intermediate hosts of the dog tapeworm, developing liver and lung cysts with daughter cysts and hydatid sand. Casoni test is obsolete; aspiration risks anaphylaxis and dissemination.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Helminths: intestinal & tissue nematodes, cestodes, trematodes
questions.stem: Iron deficiency anaemia from intestinal blood loss is characteristic of infection with:
questions.concept: Hookworm larvae penetrate skin causing ground itch, migrate through lungs and attach to duodenal mucosa sucking blood, causing hypochromic microcytic anaemia and hypoproteinaemia. Albendazole with iron is the treatment.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Helminths: intestinal & tissue nematodes, cestodes, trematodes
questions.stem: Perianal itching worse at night in a child, diagnosed by the cellophane tape test, indicates:
questions.concept: The female worm migrates to the perianal skin at night to lay eggs, causing pruritus ani. The NIH cellophane swab taken in the morning before washing is diagnostic; the whole family is treated to prevent reinfection.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Helminths: intestinal & tissue nematodes, cestodes, trematodes
questions.stem: Loeffler syndrome, transient pulmonary infiltrates with eosinophilia, is caused by larval migration of:
questions.concept: Larvae passing through the pulmonary capillaries into alveoli provoke an eosinophilic inflammatory response with migratory infiltrates, cough and wheeze, resolving as migration completes.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Helminths: intestinal & tissue nematodes, cestodes, trematodes
questions.stem: The drug of choice for most intestinal nematode infections is:
questions.concept: Albendazole and mebendazole inhibit tubulin polymerisation and cover ascaris, hookworm, whipworm and pinworm - the basis of mass deworming. Praziquantel is used for cestodes and trematodes, ivermectin for strongyloides and onchocerciasis.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Helminths: intestinal & tissue nematodes, cestodes, trematodes
questions.stem: Autoinfection allowing lifelong persistence and hyperinfection in the immunosuppressed is characteristic of:
questions.concept: Strongyloides larvae can mature within the host and reinvade, so infection persists for decades. Corticosteroids or HTLV-1 infection precipitate hyperinfection with disseminated larvae and Gram-negative sepsis, often fatal.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Helminths: intestinal & tissue nematodes, cestodes, trematodes
questions.stem: Cysticercosis of the eye is important because:
options: Antihelminthic treatment can provoke severe inflammation and blindness, so ocular disease must be excluded first
questions.concept: Killing an intraocular cyst releases antigens causing intense uveitis, so fundoscopy is mandatory before starting albendazole for neurocysticercosis, and corticosteroids are given alongside to limit inflammation.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Helminths: intestinal & tissue nematodes, cestodes, trematodes
questions.stem: Katayama fever, an acute hypersensitivity illness with fever, urticaria and eosinophilia, occurs in:
questions.concept: Katayama syndrome is an immune complex reaction to migrating schistosomules weeks after exposure to fresh water. Chronic schistosomiasis causes hepatic fibrosis or, with S. haematobium, bladder squamous carcinoma.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.topic: Helminths: intestinal & tissue nematodes, cestodes, trematodes
questions.stem: Praziquantel acts by:
options: Increasing membrane permeability to calcium causing tetanic contraction of the parasite
questions.concept: Calcium influx causes spastic paralysis and tegumental damage exposing parasite antigens to host immunity. It is the drug of choice for schistosomiasis, taeniasis, and neurocysticercosis alongside albendazole.
